title: Rights Issues, Salient Features & Political System

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993:
1. It defines human rights as the rights relating to life, liberty, equality and dignity of the individual guaranteed by the Constitution or embodied in international covenants and enforceable by courts in India.
2. It provides for the Human Rights Courts at the district level, specified by the State Government with the concurrence of the Chief Justice of the High Court.
3. The NHRC has the power to impose penalties on public servants found guilty of violating human rights.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Section 2(d) gives the definition, and Section 30 lets a State specify a Sessions Court as a Human Rights Court with the Chief Justice's concurrence. The NHRC can only recommend action and cannot punish, which is why it is often called a toothless body.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, National Human Rights Commission; Human Rights

questions.q: Which one of the following international instruments was adopted by the UN General Assembly on 10 December 1948?
o: International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights
Convention on the Rights of the Child
Convention on the Elimination of All Forms of Discrimination against Women
questions.e: The UDHR was adopted on 10 December 1948, which is why Human Rights Day is observed on that date. The two Covenants were adopted in 1966, CEDAW in 1979 and the CRC in 1989; the UDHR is not a binding treaty.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about protection of women at the workplace:
1. The Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013 requires every employer with ten or more employees to set up an Internal Complaints Committee.
2. The Vishaka guidelines were laid down by the Supreme Court in the absence of a statute on the subject.
3. District Officers are required to constitute a Local Committee for workplaces that have fewer than ten employees.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Supreme Court in Vishaka v. State of Rajasthan (1997) issued guidelines to fill a legislative gap, and Parliament later enacted the 2013 law. The Act requires an Internal Committee for offices with ten or more workers and a Local Committee at the district level for the rest.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Constitution (One Hundred and Sixth Amendment) Act, 2023, known as the Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam:
1. It provides for the reservation of one-third of seats for women in the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies.
2. It also applies to the Rajya Sabha and State Legislative Councils.
3. Its reservation will come into effect only after delimitation exercise undertaken following the first Census taken after its commencement.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The Act reserves one-third seats in the Lok Sabha, State Assemblies and the Delhi Assembly, including within the seats reserved for SCs and STs. It does not cover the Rajya Sabha or Legislative Councils, and operation is linked to delimitation after the first Census following commencement.
questions.s: PRS Legislative Research, 106th Amendment 2023; Laxmikanth, Women's reservation

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the rights of children in India:
1. Article 21A, inserted by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002, makes free and compulsory education a Fundamental Right for children aged 6 to 14 years.
2. Article 24 prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in any occupation whatsoever.
3. The Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012 defines a child as any person below the age of 18 years.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Art 21A and the POCSO Act, 2012 are as stated. Art 24 bars employment in factories, mines or other hazardous work, not in 'any occupation whatsoever'; the wider ban up to age 14 came through the Child Labour Act, as amended in 2016.

questions.q: Under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015, a juvenile aged between 16 and 18 years who commits a heinous offence:
o: May be tried as an adult after a preliminary assessment by the Juvenile Justice Board
Is always tried as an adult in a regular court
Cannot be tried as an adult under any circumstances
May be tried as an adult only if the offence is punishable with death
questions.e: The 2015 Act, enacted after the 2012 Delhi gang rape case, lets the Board assess the child's mental and physical capacity and understanding of consequences before transfer to the Children's Court. It is not automatic, and it applies to heinous offences, which are those with a minimum punishment of seven years or more.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Rights of children; JJ Act 2015

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Judgment)
A. Shayara Bano v. Union of India
B. K. S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India
C. National Legal Services Authority v. Union of India
D. Navtej Singh Johar v. Union of India
List-II (Subject)
1. Recognition of the third gender
2. Declared talaq-e-biddat (instant triple talaq) unconstitutional
3. Decriminalised consensual same-sex relations between adults
4. Right to privacy as a Fundamental Right
Which one of the following is the correct matching?
questions.e: Shayara Bano (2017) set aside instant triple talaq; Puttaswamy (2017) held privacy to be part of Art 21; NALSA (2014) recognised the transgender community as a third gender; Navtej Singh Johar (2018) read down Section 377 IPC for consensual adult acts.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about minority rights under the Constitution:
1. Article 29(1) protects the right of any section of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture to conserve it.
2. Article 30(1) gives all minorities, based on religion or language, the right to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice.
3. Article 29(2) allows a State-aided educational institution to deny admission on the ground of religion if it is run by a minority.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Art 29(1) is wider than Art 30 as it is available to any section of citizens, not only minorities. Art 29(2) bars denial of admission to a State-aided institution on grounds of religion, race, caste or language, and it applies to minority institutions as well.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016 is correct?
o: It recognises 7 categories of disabilities and provides 3 per cent reservation in government posts
It recognises 21 categories of disabilities and provides 10 per cent reservation in government posts
It recognises 21 categories of disabilities and provides 4 per cent reservation in government posts
It applies only to persons with 40 per cent or more benchmark disability and is silent on reservation in higher education
questions.e: The 2016 Act, passed to give effect to the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, raised the categories from 7 to 21 and the government job reservation from 3 per cent to 4 per cent. It also provides 5 per cent reservation in higher educational institutions for benchmark disabilities.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Rights of persons with disabilities; RPwD Act 2016

questions.q:
Statement-I: Under the Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017, a woman with two surviving children is entitled to 26 weeks of paid maternity leave.
Statement-II: The Act provides 26 weeks of leave for the first two children and reduces it to 12 weeks for a third child.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
questions.e: The 26 weeks apply to the first two children, so a woman who already has two surviving children gets only 12 weeks for the third. Statement-I describes the wrong situation, while Statement-II is right.
questions.s: Maternity Benefit (Amendment) Act, 2017; Laxmikanth, Rights of women

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019:
1. It provides that a person is to be recognised as transgender on the basis of a certificate of identity issued by the District Magistrate.
2. It prohibits discrimination against transgender persons in education, employment and healthcare.
3. It was enacted before the Supreme Court recognised the third gender in NALSA v. Union of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: The 2019 Act provides identity certificates from the District Magistrate and bars discrimination in education, employment and healthcare. NALSA was decided in 2014, five years before the Act, so statement 3 is wrong.
questions.s: PRS Legislative Research, Transgender Persons Act 2019; Laxmikanth, Rights of vulnerable sections

questions.q: India's accession to or ratification of which of the following international human rights instruments took place in 1979?
o: Convention on the Rights of the Child and CEDAW
Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities
International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights and International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights
questions.e: India acceded to both 1966 Covenants in 1979. The CRC was ratified in 1992, CEDAW in 1993 and the CRPD in 2007.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Human Rights; NCERT Class XI Political Theory (Rights)

questions.q: Which one of the following statements regarding the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act, 2019 is correct?
o: It repeals the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Divorce) Act, 1986 in full
It was passed before the Shayara Bano judgment
It makes the pronouncement of instant triple talaq void and illegal and makes it a punishable offence
It applies only to marriages solemnised after its commencement
questions.e: The 2019 Act makes talaq-e-biddat void and illegal, with imprisonment up to three years. It came after Shayara Bano (2017) and does not repeal the 1986 Act, which followed the Shah Bano case.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Rights of women; Muslim Women Act 2019

questions.q:
Which of the following features of the Indian Constitution is borrowed from the Government of India Act, 1935?
1. Federal scheme
2. Office of the Governor
3. Public Service Commissions
4. Fundamental Duties
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The 1935 Act supplied the federal scheme, office of the Governor, Public Service Commissions, emergency provisions and much of the administrative detail. Fundamental Duties came from the Constitution of the USSR through the 42nd Amendment.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Making of the Constitution; Salient features

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Feature)
A. Concurrent List
B. Directive Principles of State Policy
C. Suspension of Fundamental Rights during Emergency
D. Residuary powers with the Centre
List-II (Source)
1. Ireland
2. Weimar Constitution of Germany
3. Constitution of Canada
4. Constitution of Australia
Which one of the following is the correct matching?
questions.e: Australia gave the Concurrent List, Ireland the DPSP, Germany's Weimar Constitution the suspension of rights in an emergency, and Canada the strong Centre with residuary powers.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Salient features; Sources of the Constitution
questions.h: Ireland gave Directives; Canada gave a strong Centre

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Preamble:
1. The words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' were added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.
2. In the Berubari Union case (1960), the Supreme Court held that the Preamble is a part of the Constitution.
3. In the Kesavananda Bharati case (1973), the Supreme Court held that the Preamble can be amended under Article 368 without altering its basic features.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 42nd Amendment added the three words. In Berubari the Court held the Preamble was NOT part of the Constitution, and Kesavananda reversed this, so it is amendable but not so as to destroy the basic structure.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements regarding the doctrine of basic structure is correct?
o: It was first laid down by the Supreme Court in Golaknath v. State of Punjab (1967)
It is explicitly listed in Article 368
It was rejected by the Supreme Court in Minerva Mills (1980)
The Supreme Court in Kesavananda Bharati (1973) held that Parliament's power to amend does not extend to altering the basic structure of the Constitution
questions.e: A 13-judge bench in Kesavananda held 7-6 that Parliament cannot damage the basic structure. Golaknath held Parliament could not amend Fundamental Rights at all, and Minerva Mills (1980) reaffirmed basic structure by striking down parts of the 42nd Amendment.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Amendment of the Constitution; Basic structure

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the making of the Constitution:
1. The Drafting Committee was set up on 29 August 1947 with B. R. Ambedkar as its Chairman.
2. The Objectives Resolution was moved by Jawaharlal Nehru in the Constituent Assembly.
3. The Constitution was adopted on 26 November 1949 and came into force on 26 January 1950, although some provisions applied from the date of adoption.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: All three are accurate. Provisions on citizenship, elections and provisional Parliament were effective from 26 November 1949, and the rest from 26 January 1950, chosen because of the 1930 Purna Swaraj Day.

questions.q: Which one of the following schedules was added to the Constitution by the 73rd Amendment Act, 1992?
questions.e: The 73rd Amendment added the Eleventh Schedule with 29 subjects for Panchayats, and the 74th added the Twelfth Schedule with 18 subjects for municipalities. The Ninth Schedule came with the First Amendment (1951) and the Tenth with the 52nd Amendment (1985).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the amendment procedure under Article 368:
1. A Bill to amend the Constitution can be introduced only in either House of Parliament and not in a State Legislature.
2. An amendment that changes the representation of States in Parliament needs ratification by the legislatures of at least half of the States.
3. The President can withhold assent to a Constitution Amendment Bill passed in accordance with Article 368.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Only Parliament can initiate an amendment, and federal features like the representation of States need ratification by half of the State legislatures. After the 24th Amendment (1971) the President must give assent to a duly passed amendment Bill, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q: Which one of the following best explains why India is described as 'a Union of States' in Article 1 and not as a 'federation of States'?
o: States can alter the boundaries of the Union by their own legislation
Parliament cannot change the name of a State
The States have exclusive powers over all subjects, including defence
States have no right to secede, and the Union is not the result of an agreement among the States
questions.e: Dr Ambedkar explained that the Indian federation is not the result of an agreement among the units and the units have no freedom to secede. This is why the Centre can reorganise States under Arts 3 and 4, with Parliament, not the State, deciding.

questions.q: The voting age in India was reduced from 21 years to 18 years by which of the following?
questions.e: The 61st Amendment (1988) lowered the voting age under Art 326 to 18 years, which added a large number of young voters. It was given effect in 1989.

questions.q:
Consider the following features of the Indian Constitution:
1. Fundamental Rights
2. Independence of the judiciary
3. Judicial review
4. Parliamentary form of government
How many of the above are borrowed from the Constitution of the United States of America?
questions.e: Fundamental Rights, independence of the judiciary and judicial review are American features. The parliamentary system, the rule of law and the Cabinet system are British.

questions.q: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the Indian Constitution as laid down originally?
o: Separation of powers in the strict sense between the legislature and the executive
questions.e: India follows the Westminster model in which the executive is drawn from and responsible to the legislature, so there is no strict separation. Single citizenship and an integrated judicial system are the Constitution's unitary features, and the parliamentary form is an original feature.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005:
1. It extends protection to women living in a relationship in the nature of marriage.
2. A complaint can be filed only by the wife and not by any other woman in the household.
3. A Magistrate can pass protection orders and residence orders under the Act.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Act covers wives, live-in partners, sisters, mothers and other women in a shared household, so a complaint is not limited to wives. Magistrates can grant protection, residence, monetary and custody orders, and Protection Officers are appointed to assist.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Rights of women; Domestic Violence Act 2005

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Constituent Assembly:
1. Its first meeting was held on 9 December 1946 with Sachchidananda Sinha as the temporary President.
2. Dr Rajendra Prasad was elected its permanent President on 11 December 1946.
3. Its members were directly elected by the people on the basis of universal adult franchise.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Assembly met first on 9 December 1946 and chose Rajendra Prasad as President two days later. Its members were elected indirectly by the provincial legislative assemblies, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q: Which one of the following was NOT done by the 42nd Constitution Amendment Act, 1976?
o: Removal of the right to property from the list of Fundamental Rights
Insertion of Fundamental Duties as Part IV-A
Addition of the words 'Socialist', 'Secular' and 'Integrity' to the Preamble
Extension of Article 31C to give primacy to all Directive Principles over certain Fundamental Rights
questions.e: The right to property ceased to be a Fundamental Right through the 44th Amendment (1978), which put it in Art 300A as a legal right. The 42nd Amendment's expansion of Art 31C was struck down in Minerva Mills (1980).
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Amendment of the Constitution; 42nd and 44th Amendments

questions.q: In I. R. Coelho v. State of Tamil Nadu (2007), the Supreme Court held that laws placed in the Ninth Schedule:
o: Are completely immune from judicial review as per Article 31B
Before 1951 can be reviewed on any ground of violation of Fundamental Rights
Can be reviewed only by a bench of at least seven judges
After 24 April 1973 are open to judicial review on the ground that they damage the basic structure
questions.e: A nine-judge bench held that Art 31B cannot be a way to destroy the basic structure, and fixed the date of the Kesavananda judgment (24 April 1973) as the cut-off. Laws placed in the Schedule after that date can be tested against the basic structure.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Fundamental Duties:
1. They were incorporated on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee.
2. They are justiciable in the same way as Fundamental Rights.
3. The duty of a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to a child aged 6 to 14 years was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.
4. They are placed in Part IV of the Constitution.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Swaran Singh Committee (1976) recommended them, and Art 51A(k) was added in 2002. Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable and are in Part IV-A (Art 51A), not Part IV.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 is correct?
o: It requires private unaided non-minority schools to reserve 25 per cent of seats at entry level for children from weaker and disadvantaged sections
It extends free and compulsory education to all children from 3 to 18 years
It was enacted before Article 21A was inserted into the Constitution
Its reservation requirement applies equally to minority institutions
questions.e: Section 12(1)(c) imposes the 25 per cent reservation, and the Supreme Court upheld it for non-minority private unaided schools in 2012. Art 21A was inserted in 2002 and the Act followed in 2009; the Act covers ages 6 to 14.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Tenth Schedule (anti-defection law):
1. A member elected as an independent is disqualified if he joins a political party after the election.
2. A nominated member is disqualified if he joins a political party within six months of taking his seat.
3. A member is disqualified if he votes or abstains contrary to the party direction without prior permission, unless the party condones the act within 15 days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: A nominated member may join a party within six months, and is disqualified only if he joins after that period. The independent and whip-violation rules are as stated.

questions.q:
Statement-I: After the 91st Amendment Act, 2003, a defection by one-third of the members of a legislature party does not protect them from disqualification.
Statement-II: The Tenth Schedule now protects only a merger agreed to by not less than two-thirds of the members of the legislature party.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
questions.e: The 91st Amendment deleted the provision protecting a split by one-third of a legislature party, leaving only merger protection with a two-thirds requirement. That is why a one-third split is no longer a safe route.

questions.q: In Kihoto Hollohan v. Zachillhu (1992), the Supreme Court held that:
o: The Tenth Schedule violates the legislator's freedom of speech and is invalid in its entirety
The Tenth Schedule is valid, but the Speaker's decision on disqualification is subject to judicial review
The Speaker's decision on disqualification is final and cannot be challenged in any court
Disqualification under the Tenth Schedule is decided by the President on the advice of the Election Commission
questions.e: The Court upheld the Schedule, held that Para 7, which barred court jurisdiction, needed ratification by States and was invalid, and said the Speaker acts as a tribunal. The President-Election Commission route applies to disqualifications under Art 103, not the Tenth Schedule.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about disqualification under the Representation of the People Act, 1951:
1. In Lily Thomas v. Union of India (2013), the Supreme Court struck down the provision that allowed a convicted legislator to continue in office pending appeal.
2. A person convicted and sentenced to imprisonment for two years or more is disqualified from the date of conviction and for six years after release.
3. Disqualification applies only if the sentence is for five years or more.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Section 8(4) was struck down in 2013, so disqualification takes effect upon conviction. Section 8(3) sets the threshold at two years, not five.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Electoral reforms; Representation of the People Act

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about NOTA (None of the Above):
1. It was introduced following the Supreme Court's directions in PUCL v. Union of India (2013).
2. If NOTA gets the highest number of votes in a constituency, the election is countermanded.
3. The Supreme Court has held that NOTA is not available in Rajya Sabha elections.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: NOTA gives voters a way to reject all candidates, but it has no effect on results: the candidate with the most votes among the contestants wins. In 2018 the Court held that NOTA cannot be used in Rajya Sabha polls where open ballot applies, to prevent horse-trading and defections.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about electronic voting in India:
1. EVMs were used in all constituencies in the Lok Sabha elections of 2004.
2. The Supreme Court in Subramanian Swamy v. Election Commission of India (2013) directed that VVPAT be introduced.
3. EVMs were first used in an election in 1982 in a by-election in Assam.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: EVMs were first used in the 1982 by-election at Paravur in Kerala, not Assam. The 2004 general election was the first fully on EVMs, and the VVPAT followed the 2013 judgment.

questions.q: In February 2024, a five-judge Bench of the Supreme Court struck down the Electoral Bond Scheme. Which one of the following was the main ground?
o: It violated the federal structure by taking away the States' power over party funding
It violated Article 301 on the freedom of trade and commerce
It violated the secrecy of the ballot under Article 326
It violated the voters' right to information under Article 19(1)(a) by making political funding anonymous
questions.e: The Court held that anonymous funding hindered the voter's right to know about donors to political parties, and that unlimited corporate contributions were arbitrary. It did not rely on federalism or Art 326.
questions.s: Supreme Court, Association for Democratic Reforms v. Union of India, 15 Feb 2024; The Hindu, 16 Feb 2024

questions.q:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Committee)
A. Dinesh Goswami Committee
B. Indrajit Gupta Committee
C. Vohra Committee
D. Tarkunde Committee
List-II (Subject)
1. State funding of elections
2. Nexus between criminals, politicians and bureaucrats
3. Electoral reforms report of 1990
4. Citizens' committee on electoral reforms set up by Jayaprakash Narayan
Which one of the following is the correct matching?
questions.e: The Dinesh Goswami Committee (1990) dealt with electoral reforms; the Indrajit Gupta Committee (1998) recommended partial state funding; the Vohra Committee (1993) examined the criminal-politician nexus; and the Tarkunde Committee (1974) was set up by JP.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the recognition of a political party as a national party under the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968:
1. A party that is recognised as a State party in four or more States qualifies.
2. A party that wins at least 2 per cent of the Lok Sabha seats from at least three different States qualifies.
3. A party that is registered with the Election Commission under Section 29A of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 automatically qualifies.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Registration under Section 29A is only the first step and gives no recognition. Recognition depends on the performance tests in the Symbols Order.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about delimitation:
1. The orders of the Delimitation Commission have the force of law and cannot be questioned in any court.
2. The 84th Amendment Act, 2001 extended the freeze on readjustment of seats in Lok Sabha and State Assemblies until the first Census taken after 2026.
3. The 87th Amendment Act, 2003 provided that delimitation would be based on the 2011 Census.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Delimitation orders are immune from court challenge, and the freeze originally imposed by the 42nd Amendment was extended by the 84th. The 87th Amendment changed the base from the 1991 to the 2001 Census for readjustment within States, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about election disputes:
1. Doubts and disputes relating to the election of the President are inquired into and decided by the Supreme Court.
2. An election petition against the election of a member of the Lok Sabha is filed directly before the Supreme Court.
3. Article 329 bars courts from questioning an election except by an election petition.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Art 71 gives the Supreme Court exclusive jurisdiction over President and Vice-President election disputes. For Parliament and State Legislatures, election petitions go to the High Court, with an appeal to the Supreme Court.

questions.q: A candidate in a Lok Sabha election forfeits the security deposit if he or she fails to secure at least:
o: One-third of the total valid votes polled
One-tenth of the total votes in the electoral roll
One-fourth of the total valid votes polled
One-sixth of the total valid votes polled in the constituency
questions.e: Section 158 of the Representation of the People Act, 1951 provides forfeiture if the candidate gets no more than one-sixth of valid votes, which discourages non-serious candidates.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Elections; Representation of the People Act

questions.q: According to Gabriel Almond's classification of interest groups, which one of the following is an anomic group?
o: A spontaneous group formed during a riot or violent demonstration
A bureaucracy or army acting as a group
questions.e: Anomic groups arise spontaneously, as in riots and demonstrations, and lack organisation. Trade unions are associational, caste and kinship groups are non-associational, and bureaucracy and army are institutional.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Pressure groups in India do not themselves contest elections.
Statement-II: Pressure groups aim to influence public policy and not to capture political power.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: A group that only wants to shape policy has no need to field candidates, whereas political parties contest elections to capture power. This is the basic distinction between pressure groups and parties.

questions.q:
Consider the following pairs of trade unions and their year of founding:
1. All India Trade Union Congress : 1920
2. Indian National Trade Union Congress : 1947
3. Bharatiya Mazdoor Sangh : 1955
4. Centre of Indian Trade Unions : 1960
How many of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
questions.e: AITUC (1920) is the oldest central union, INTUC was formed in 1947 and BMS in 1955. CITU was formed in 1970 after the CPI split, not 1960.

questions.q: Which one of the following business associations was founded in 1927 at the initiative of G. D. Birla and Purshottamdas Thakurdas?
o: Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry of India
Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry
questions.e: FICCI came out of the nationalist business class's wish for an Indian-led body alongside the British-dominated chambers. ASSOCHAM was set up in 1920.

questions.q: Which State had the first non-Congress government after independence, elected in 1957 and dismissed in 1959 under Article 356?
questions.e: The Communist Party of India government under E. M. S. Namboodiripad took office in Kerala in 1957 and was dismissed in 1959 amid the 'Liberation Struggle'.
questions.h: 1957 Kerala: elected communist ministry, dismissed under Art 356 in 1959

questions.q: The phrase 'Aaya Ram Gaya Ram', which came to symbolise political defections, is associated with the 1967 events in which State?
questions.e: In 1967 Haryana MLA Gaya Lal reportedly changed his party several times in a single day. The wave of defections after the 1967 elections led to the Y. B. Chavan Committee (1969) and eventually the Tenth Schedule in 1985.

questions.q: In Keisham Meghachandra Singh v. Speaker, Manipur Legislative Assembly (2020), the Supreme Court:
o: Held that Speakers should ordinarily decide disqualification petitions within three months and suggested that Parliament consider an independent tribunal for such decisions
Held that the Speaker has no role in deciding disqualification under the Tenth Schedule
Held that the Governor should decide disqualification petitions
Held that the Tenth Schedule does not apply to the legislators who vote against party whip
questions.e: The Court said delay by the Speaker defeats the purpose of the anti-defection law, and urged Parliament to consider handing the task to a permanent tribunal headed by a retired judge. It did not remove the Speaker's role.
questions.s: Supreme Court, Keisham Meghachandra Singh (21 Jan 2020); The Hindu, 22 Jan 2020

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Model Code of Conduct (MCC):
1. It is a statutory code enforceable by courts under the Representation of the People Act, 1951.
2. It comes into force from the date the Election Commission announces the election schedule.
3. It restricts the ruling party from using official machinery for campaigning.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The MCC is a consensus-based, non-statutory code that the ECI enforces through its powers under Art 324, so statement 1 is wrong. It starts at the announcement of the schedule and bars misuse of official resources by the party in power.
questions.s: Laxmikanth, Elections; Model Code of Conduct
